At first glance, sharpening a knife is very simple - you just want to cut the steel along the edge of he knife into a nice V shape. That's really all there is to it.

In practice, it's a little tricky. In order to get that nice V you have to grind the metal away at a very consistent angle. You can do it by sweeping the blade across a grinding stone but maintaining the exact angle for every stroke is hard. If you mess it up, you'll end up with a U instead of a V and the knife won't be sharp.

https://lansky.com/files/4414/0872/2701/Clamp_in_use.jpg

Here you see a knife held in a clamp, and the clamp is mounted on a little stand. The red angled piece is a grind stone, and it's held at the correct angle while in use. Mom helped me grow fresh greens to feed him. I had to learn to groom him and trim his claws. I had to search around the house for things he might want to chew and move it out his way. I took very good care of this one and he lived about 8 years. I always had puppies and kittens to rear and train.

When I was about 10, many members started seriously encouraging me to help take care of little cousins. When someone had a new baby, all the kids, I have tons of cousins, would be brought along to attend the birth. We would be sat down, and someone would help us hold the new baby and help change diapers and how to feed them. My family is very good about not waiting for you to ask questions and just explaining things. "This is how babies need to sleep and this is why...this is what this cry means...this is what baby poops are like...this is what to do when baby is stressing you." We were never scolded for trying to interact with new babies, just monitored.

I started being allowed to watch toddler cousins around this age for short periods of time while the parents did chores in other parts of the house. Because I had small animals before, I already had a clear understanding of baby-ness and I knew what types of things they will try to get into. Babies are curious people and hearing no all the time is bad for them so a safe place for them to play and explore freely must be made.

I was a gradual build from there and by the time I was a teenager I could be watching 4 or 5 little ones by myself on the weekends. I knew how to discipline them, keep them happy, teach them, schedule, nap them, nurse illnesses and put them to bed.

Thanks family for doing me a solid.

I guess first I had a cat that I took pretty good care of and loved on so much.
Once my aunts had kids since I was the oldest I would keep an eye on them or take them to the park while the adults hung out or worked. I would also babysit them.
In high school I had a few babysitting jobs and after highschool I worked full time at two daycares before having kids. The first daycare I worked with a women who had lots of excerince and schooling and was just above and beyond at her job. I observed her closely and learned a lot from her.
I'm greatful for all the chances I had to work with children before having my own but in so many ways it did not prepare me having my own.
Tiny humans are crazy. Even if you have a vague idea of what you are doing, they have their own temperaments and ideas about things.
